newsitem.title: USA: Dominick's Q1 beats its expectations.
newsitem.headline: Dominick's Q1 beats its expectations.

text.p: Dominick's Supermarkets Inc said Tuesday its fiscal first quarter earnings and operating cash flow performance "well exceeded" its expectations.

However, comparable store sales declined "somewhat" during the quarter due to the substantially greater remodeling activity compared to recent quarters. That caused some disruption in 12 stores, Dominick's said.
It added that a shortened holiday season also impacted same store sales.

Earlier, Dominick's reported earnings for the first quarter ended January 25 of $0.23 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.05, which included $1.5 million in preferred stock accretion expense.

Dominick's said it generated record operating cash flow of $35.9 million for the first quarter, or six percent of sales. A year ago, its operating cash flow was $29.9 million, or 5.1 percent of sales.
Dominick's said its has experienced strong acceptance of its "Fresh Values" customer card, which was introduced during the quarter. The Fresh Values card offers special pricing for customers.

"As this was our first quarter as a public company, we conservatively approached the introduction of our Fresh Values card," president Robert Mariano said in a statement. "As a result, we believe cash flow results were stronger than would have been the case had the company been more promotional during the introductory phase of the card program."

He added that the company's main goal over the next several quarters will be to use the data collected through the card program to develop aggressive marketing programs tailored to customers' buying patterns.
